facts.about: Central Depository Services Limited is a Market Infrastructure Institution (MII), part of the capital market structure, providing services to all market participants - exchanges, clearing corporations, depository participants (DPs), issuers and investors. It is a facilitator for holding of securities in the dematerialised form and an enabler for securities transactions.

flags.text: Profit compounding (+18%/yr) lags sales (+27%/yr) over 3 years — margins under pressure
Operating margin compressed 6 pts in 3 years (57% → 51%)

business.summary: CDSL provides secure, efficient depository services, enabling dematerialisation and digitisation of securities. It supports India's securities markets through technology-driven infrastructure, offering services like e-CAS, e-DIS, and online account opening to empower investors and intermediaries.

segments.name: Depository Activity
segments.note: Provides depository services for securities in electronic form.

segments.name: Data Entry and Storage
segments.note: Centralized record keeping of KYC documents for capital market investors.

segments.name: Repository
segments.note: Electronic storage for insurance policies and warehouse receipts.

narrative.scoreline: Management has successfully defended its dominant market share and top-line growth, but aggressive technology spending and regulatory pricing resets are visibly eroding operating margins.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Technology is the core DNA requiring continuous investment regardless of market cycles.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Other expenses and technology costs have risen, contributing to a margin drop from 60% in FY24 to 51% in FY26.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Employee cost increases are primarily driven by annual appraisal cycles and variable pay.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Net profit fell from ₹526 cr in FY25 to ₹455 cr in FY26 as costs outpaced revenue growth.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Revenue impact from price reductions was partially offset by higher fetch volumes.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Revenue growth slowed significantly in FY26 (5.8%) compared to FY25 (48.6%).

bull: Revenue reached a record ₹394 cr in Sep 2026, representing 23.5% year-on-year growth.
Strong cash generation with a 5-year cash conversion rate at 97% of PAT.
Dominant market position maintained with over 80% share in demat accounts.
bear: Operating margins have compressed 9 percentage points over the last two fiscal years to 51%.
Profit compounding at 18% over three years is significantly lagging sales growth of 27%.
Regulatory pricing resets in the KRA segment have created a visible drag on revenue momentum.
watch: Sustainability of the 58% margin achieved in the Sep 2026 quarter.
Growth in pledge income relative to MTF book expansion.
Impact of Search API charges on offsetting KRA fee reductions.

claims.claim: Management continues to invest in technology to ensure system resilience and efficiency as market activity evolves.
claims.quote: We continue to embark on this journey to ensure that the robustness and the resiliency of the CDSL system remains top notch and continues to work on that.

claims.claim: The rack rates for KRA services are INR5 for creation and INR28 for fetching.
claims.quote: For creation, it has come down to INR5. And for fetching it has come down to INR28.

claims.claim: Higher KRA expenses are driven by increased interoperability costs and Aadhaar-based eKYC charges payable to UIDAI.
claims.quote: On the KRA side, the other expenses have increased primarily because the interoperability expenses have increased with the increase in fetch volumes. Point number two is we also do e-sign.

claims.claim: The company does not internally track or separate corporate action revenue from IPO-related revenue.
claims.quote: We internally do not monitor as to what would be corporate action revenue, what would be IPO-related revenue etc. Basically, it's a total revenue set for us.

claims.claim: The company prioritizes infrastructure and technology to maintain value proposition, regardless of quarter-on-quarter fluctuations.
claims.quote: It will be difficult to comment whether the technology spend will grow or not grow in future. One is we don't give forward-looking statements.

claims.claim: CDSL focuses on long-term sustainable growth and value proposition rather than quarter-on-quarter market share metrics.
claims.quote: our intent at least CDSL is not a quarter-on-quarter growth. It is a long-term sustainable growth, which creates value proposition for the market.

claims.claim: Revenue impact from SEBI-mandated price reductions was partially offset by higher fetch volumes and new Search API charges.
claims.quote: One was the higher fetch volumes. – Further, when the charges were reduced by SEBI, they had allowed us to charge on the Search API, which again gave us some revenue

claims.claim: Quarter-on-quarter increases in employee costs are primarily driven by the annual appraisal cycle and variable pay payouts.
claims.quote: the appraisal has got done in this quarter, which has just ended, and all the variable pay, et cetera, is paid in this quarter.

claims.claim: Technology is the core DNA of the business, requiring continuous investment to maintain scalability and value proposition.
claims.quote: I think one needs to see this business, and I have been talking about this, that technology is the DNA of our business. It's kind of the Raw Material, Work in Progress, and Finished goods.

claims.claim: CDSL maintains a dominant market share of over 80% in demat accounts.
claims.quote: maintaining our 80% plus market share with a consistently incremental market share of 85% to 90%, supported by the continuous trust of investors and depository participants on our platform.

claims.claim: The reduction in KYC fetch and creation charges is an industry-wide regulatory change.
claims.quote: It's going to be across basically the industry. So, it is not only for CVL.

claims.claim: Pricing changes require SEBI approval and are focused on inclusivity and maintaining a competitive value proposition.
claims.quote: So, it's giving lower cost for inclusivity for more and more players to come into the fold, but also not compromising on the quality, which is getting given to such people at a lower cost.

claims.claim: Infrastructure investment is necessary to maintain a seamless experience and keep pace with innovation, AI, and regulatory requirements.
claims.quote: The process of ensuring that a seamless experience is there for all the participants is our intent and all basically will be able to see their holdings, etc., in a very seamless manner.

claims.claim: Additions of unlisted companies are circumstance-driven, occurring primarily when companies need to raise or transfer capital.
claims.quote: But again, those conditions remain only when they want to raise capital, or they want to transfer capital. So those are very circumstance driven as to when they are mandated to be registered with us.

claims.claim: The company must maintain prepared infrastructure regardless of market cycles to handle sudden growth spurts.
claims.quote: As a market infrastructure provider, we are continuing to build on our systems, whether we have a great period or a lean period because when the growth comes, it comes all of a sudden.

claims.claim: The company maintains that there has been no significant drop in market share, attributing fluctuations to seasonal circumstances.
claims.quote: So, there has been no significant drop as I would see it as of now.

risks.text: Contingent liabilities include bank guarantees totaling 710.46 Lakh as of March 31, 2026.
Related party transactions include purchases (0.29%) and sales (0.46%) of total values.
Auditor identified IT systems and controls as a key audit matter due to transaction volume.
